Window 1 holds: when no marker ref exists, the function returns at `!present` before the attestation is read, and the next record overwrites the orphaned value. INFO (non-blocking NIT) — materialize.go:160 still wraps aerr in next.RenderBDError explicitly, but completeMergeMetadataFn now defaults to mergeMetadataEscaped, which already applies it. So the production chain renders through renderBDError twice. This is safe: ASCII control-escaped lines and force-quoted recovery lines come out the same on the second pass. Because termsafe.Escape is not idempotent on lines containing printable non-ASCII runes (strconv.Quote keeps them and the second pass re-quotes), such lines get double-quoted. The effect is cosmetic, not a safety issue. The explicit wrap could be dropped, or kept as defense for test seams that swap in a raw function.
